doctrine: Higgsfield is a unified AI production studio (Jan-Apr 2026 content). Architecture separates Features (workflow tools: Popcorn storyboard, Cinema Studio, Earn platform, Vibe Motion) from Models (AI engines: WAN 2.6, Seedance 2.0, Kling 2.6/3.0, Minimax Hailuo, Soul, Reef, VEO 3.1). Core operator thesis: character consistency + daily posting consistency = earnings. Earn platform closes the loop: post content, receive payment in a single workflow. Proof case: mushroom-character AI influencer, 180K followers in 3 weeks, brand deals by week 5.
operating_rules: Start/End Frames: lock Start frame (establishes location/character look), lock End frame (clean finish for cut, thumbnail, CTA)
Screenshot-as-reference: grab any frame from previous video, paste as Start or End constraint in next generation (frame-level storyboarding without the storyboard tool)
Consistency-first: build character keyframe + prop sheet BEFORE generating any scene
Character Sheet as database: generate once, use as persistent identity entry (face variants, outfit options, physical traits) across hundreds of scenes without retraining
Tagging system: reference uploaded assets via @image[n] or @reference syntax to force coherence across multi-scene prompts
Master Image Anchor: single high-quality portrait as persistent reference for every multi-scene project
Storyboard-First Discipline: never go straight to video; define frame sequence using Popcorn storyboard tool first
Many-to-Few Selection: generate 5-10 takes per shot; curate best snippets in post; expect and budget for 30-50% failure rate
Editing vs Generating: spend 80% of time selecting best segments, not chasing the perfect AI clip in one pass
Constraint Prompting: use simple prompts; let Director settings (Genre/Budget/Era/Archetype) carry the configuration load
Asset Reusability: create Elements (characters, locations) once; permute across scenes infinitely
Re-run + Re-edit Loop: on failure, either re-run for a different output OR edit the prompt in an LLM to fix the specific issue then re-run
Audio De-noising: separate audio from AI video in CapCut to strip unwanted AI-generated sound effects
Multi-shot Manual Mode: define shot durations explicitly (e.g., 5 sec + 7 sec = 12 sec total) for frame-level granularity
Performance-based earnings: 3 posts daily beats 1 high-quality post weekly on the Earn platform
Parallel generation: batch 5-10 scene generations per location simultaneously; select best angles post-hoc
named_methods: Popcorn Workflow: Conceptualization -> Anchor Generation -> Storyboard Expansion -> Sequential Animation -> Post-Production
AI Influencer Assembly: Persona Engineering (traits/background) -> Viral Motion Library animation -> Earn posting cadence
Cinema Director Pipeline: Casting and Asset Definition -> Scene Orchestration -> Voice Consistency -> Many-to-Few Post-Production
Fraud-casting: static image -> video animator -> 'speaking into mic, side angle, hyper-realistic' prompt -> ambient audio overlay (AI talking-head simulation)
Multi-shot Prompting: single prompt generates many consistent shots while maintaining character, location, and lighting continuity
8-Interview Discovery: ask 8-10 industry experts 'Did you see this result?' / 'How do you achieve this?' / 'What is your core limitation?' before building any product
90-Day Sprint: Day 0-30 discovery and MVP; Day 30-90 iterate to $80K/month revenue with 6-days-per-week daily shipping cadence
Click-to-Add Automation: product URL -> automated ad generation (removes scripting, filming, editing phases for e-commerce)
JSON Shot List: structure complex multi-shot sequences as JSON (shot_1_duration, shot_2_duration, etc.) for machine-readable scene definition
prompt_grammar: Core formula: Composition + Subject + Camera move + Mood (treat as shot-list framing, not conversational description)

Character detail stacking: [Age/ethnicity/build] + [hair: style/color/treatment] + [outfit: color/material/cut] in single prompt (e.g., 'Male Latino, 30, athletic, tall, hazel eyes, wavy brown hair slick back, mustache')

Location specification with mood: [Space type] + [architectural detail] + [lighting] + [atmosphere] (e.g., 'Gatsby mansion lobby, grand twin staircases, glossy marble floor, warm golden lights, elegant yet slightly ominous')
Camera directive shorthand: leave prompt body empty, select camera directive only (e.g., 'zoom in', 'pan left') for cinematography without complex prompting
LLM expansion loop: 'Give me a detailed prompt to generate a keyframe. I want [simple description].' -> paste into Claude -> use returned detailed prompt in Higgsfield
Error recovery: 'Describe the issue to LLM and make it explicit in the prompt definition, then re-run'

quality_gates: Credit expenditure gate: each scene 0.5-192 credits; audit per-project budget before attempting multi-scene narratives
Iteration tolerance gate: accept 30-50% failed generations; pre-budget for curation phase
Upscale gate: run all final outputs through Upscale before publishing to remove AI artifacting
Character consistency gate: verify face/outfit consistency across 2-3 test frames before full animation; use character sheet + Manual Mode upload constraints
Location persistence gate: use screenshot-as-reference when staying in same location; verify floor/wall textures match between shots
Animation readiness gate: keyframe must pass visual inspection with no visible morphing or skeletal artifacts before animating
Voice consistency gate: generate 10-second audio reference sample first; test custom voice clone on single short clip before full dialogue sequence
Market entry gate: conduct 8-10 expert interviews to define one specific technical limitation before building product

contradictions_to_watch: Automation vs control: platform markets 'Click-to-Add automation' but real workflow is highly manual (Director settings, prompt engineering, multi-shot curation)
Cost efficiency: '24-hour commercial under budget' claim vs actual 16-192 credits per scene across 10+ scenes adds up significantly
Character consistency: unified tagging marketed as solving consistency, yet examples show repeated morphing, skeletal artifacts, and face quality degradation
Speed vs quality: '90-Day $1M ARR' assumes daily shipping AND high-value clients, but 5-10 iterations per scene are the real norm
weird_gold: Fraud-casting is the platform's own explicit term for AI talking-head simulation, not a euphemism
Lego propaganda AI videos documented with millions of views and political impact, demonstrating AI video already weaponized at scale
JSON prompt formatting treats prompts as machine-readable code, not natural language; signals operator-tier vs consumer-tier usage
Character sheet output is functionally a database record (face variants, outfit options, physical traits) suggesting persistent identity infrastructure inside Higgsfield
Multi-reference model: single character asset scales across hundreds of videos without retraining, template-based not fine-tuning-based
Native audio + lip-sync solved at model level (Seance 2), not in post-production; removes the historic lip-sync blocker from AI video workflows
sniped_routing: Track B (AI creative engine for IG): Popcorn Workflow + Cinema Director Pipeline are the primary production stacks
Character Sheet Locking maps directly to SNIPED composite environment rotation discipline (build the world asset once, permute across chapters)
Earn platform is a monetization primitive; evaluate against SNIPED Revenue Engine before integrating

Fraud-casting technique is relevant to authority content (interview-style AI segments) but conflicts with Lineage Doctrine if applied to identity representation; use only for fictional/commercial personas
90-Day Sprint model is a separate operator playbook, not a SNIPED production cadence; useful for any AI product vertical adjacent to photography
Credit cost structure ($0.125-$192/scene) requires a budget gate before any multi-scene narrative is greenlit inside SNIPED OS
